Update: One day later, GPT-6 Astra is rolling out to Business and Pro customers on the $100 or $200 monthly plans. Other new models had launched before it, with $20 monthly Plus customers gaining access afterwards.

Update #2: A few hours later, $20 monthly Plus subscribers also gained access to Astra.

It has been just over a year since OpenAI launched its first GPT-5 models for ChatGPT. Now, the time has come for GPT-6 Astra, bringing upgrades to ChatGPT and Codex features. Here are the details.

GPT-6 Astra Details

OpenAI has officially unveiled its new model, GPT-6 Astra, calling it "the world's smartest and most aligned model."

OpenAI further explained how GPT-6 improves computer control capabilities, allowing ChatGPT to use your Mac or other desktop computers, including running in the background while you work:

OpenAI also said GPT-6 Astra is "the most capable model for software engineering to date."

For Codex, here is some new information about GPT-6:

OpenAI called GPT-6 Astra "a major leap in cybersecurity capability," noting that it "reached the Critical threshold in cybersecurity under its Preparedness Framework."

As a result, the model is rolling out to users gradually.

OpenAI said: "GPT-6 Astra is rolling out today to a limited number of organizations, and will become available to all ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users, as well as through the OpenAI API and AWS, in the coming days."

"Usage of Astra is included in existing subscription tiers, with additional usage credits available for purchase by users and businesses. GPT-6 Astra Pro is also available to users on Pro, Business, and Enterprise plans. Enterprise admins can enable Astra for their workspace; it will be off by default at launch."

The Road to GPT-6 Astra

GPT-5 launched on August 7, 2025, replacing GPT-4o and several reasoning models as ChatGPT's default. Its standout feature was automatic routing: ChatGPT could answer quickly or engage deeper reasoning depending on the request. OpenAI also claimed it hallucinated less than GPT-4o.

Apple adopted the model across iOS 26, iPadOS 26, and macOS Tahoe 26. ChatGPT requests handled through Apple Intelligence — including Siri handoffs, Writing Tools, and Visual Intelligence features — shifted from GPT-4o to GPT-5.

GPT-5.1 arrived in November with a promise of warmer, more natural responses. December's "code red" GPT-5.2 accelerated professional workflows in response to Gemini. GPT-5.3 Instant addressed ChatGPT's "cringe" tone, and two days later GPT-5.4 Thinking launched with a 1 million-token context window and built-in computer control.

OpenAI later added GPT-5.4 mini and nano, the restricted GPT-5.4-Cyber, GPT-5.5 for higher-autonomy work, GPT-5.5 Instant, and the GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna models released in July.

From Codex Mac App to the New ChatGPT

The software surrounding these models also evolved. OpenAI launched a dedicated Codex Mac app in February, serving as a hub for running multiple coding agents, reviewing changes, and scheduling work.

In July, Codex effectively became the new ChatGPT desktop app, integrating Chat, Work, and Codex features, while the original native client was renamed ChatGPT Classic.

For me, Codex changed how I use ChatGPT. I was able to offload more work that didn't require critical thinking, and even build some tools on my Mac that I otherwise couldn't have put together.

GPT-6 Availability

OpenAI said its new GPT-6 model would initially be available only to members of its cybersecurity-focused Daybreak program. This mirrors the release cadence of the previous GPT-5.6.
